AD data is empty or the first byte length is 0 — no fields to decode

Format: [length 1B][type 1B][data ...], the length byte includes the type byte itself; length 0x00 marks the end of advertising data. Out-of-range lengths are truncated to the actual remaining bytes and marked.
No fields to display — fix the input above and decode again
Paste real advertising data and tap PARSE; this page never generates sample data
128-bit UUIDs are reversed from little endian into standard UUIDs; company IDs / service UUIDs are decoded little endian too. Unknown IDs keep their raw hex — no guessing.

The radar / BLE scan page shares this AdStructureDecoder for advertising details (the main thread wires the decoder into scan details); both follow the same AD Structure rules and produce identical results.

Decoded types: Flags, 16 / 32 / 128-bit UUID lists, local name, TX power, Class of Device, connection interval range, Service Data, Appearance, advertising interval, LE device address, LE Role, URI and vendor-specific data. Unknown types show \"unknown AD type\" with raw hex.

Requests MTU 247 after connecting; the actual value comes from the system onMtuChanged callback. Reading PHY is unsupported below Android 8.0. The NUS service is 6E400001, compatible with FFE0 / FFE1 serial.
Waiting for device data — UTF-8 text notified over TX will append here
Sends write to the RX characteristic; Serial.println appends CRLF to the text. A single write must not exceed MTU-3 bytes — oversized writes are rejected explicitly, never silently truncated.
No logs yet — connection, service discovery, CCCD subscription, TX/RX and error events are all recorded here
No bonded devices — pair in system Bluetooth settings first, then refresh
Programmatic unbonding uses the hidden BluetoothDevice.removeBond() method; Android 9+ may reject it. Re-pairing is required after unbonding.
The delete action is only available for system-bonded devices; an empty list means no bonds exist.
A true return from removeBond only means the system accepted the request; the bond list is the final source of truth.
If the system restricts hidden APIs or the vendor ROM lacks removeBond, remove (\"forget\") the device in system Bluetooth settings.
Re-pairing must be confirmed in the system Bluetooth dialog; this page offers no silent pairing.
AD decode only decodes the real bytes you input; field meanings come from Bluetooth Assigned Numbers, with no business-semantic guessing.
NUS is Nordic\'s official demo service and only works with devices flashed with NUS firmware (or FFE0 / FFE1 serial firmware).
MTU / PHY are negotiated after connection; the device may reject the request or fall back to a lower tier.
Bonding relies on the hidden removeBond() method; if the system refuses, forget the device in system Bluetooth settings — this page never pretends deletion succeeded.
Bluetooth connection and pairing require the Nearby devices permission, requested through the app permission gateway.
